result.summary: JMAK devices can now receive commands over TCP and over SMS. The new class is `JmakProtocolEncoder(Protocol, boolean textChannel)`, and `JmakProtocol` registers it for both data and text commands. Over TCP a command is written `$<id>;<value>;|...#`. Over SMS it is written `JMAK#<s|e>;<id>;<value>#...`, and reboot is the literal `JMAK#REBOOT#`. Your examples come out exactly as you gave them. The full test suite and checkstyle pass when run with JDK 25. Two points to know. First, the task text had a broken spot where the TCP prefix should be; I used `$`, taken from your example `$34;1;#`. Second, Traccar has no 'movement alarm' command type. I used `alarmGeofence` for it, because the Meiligao encoder already sends its movement alarm through that type.

changes.summary: New encoder for custom, engine stop and resume, output control (index 1/2/3 maps to parameters 34/94/167), periodic positions, odometer, set connection (parameter 13 for an IPv4 address, 43 for a domain, then 12 for the port), reboot, speed limit, low battery alarm, power removal alarm and movement alarm (alarmGeofence, parameter 59). Builds the TCP or SMS format depending on textChannel.
Declares the supported data and text commands, sets the SMS encoder (textChannel=true), and adds StringEncoder and the TCP encoder (textChannel=false) to the pipeline.
Tests every supported command over TCP and over SMS, including the examples from the task.

acceptance.criterion: Commands encoded as described over TCP and SMS
acceptance.evidence: JmakProtocolEncoderTest passes. It checks `$43;jmak.com.br;|12;5259;#`, `JMAK#s;13;191.233.246.121#s;12;5259#`, `JMAK#e;57;0#`, `$34;1;#`, `JMAK#REBOOT#`, `$93;1;#` and every other supported command in both modes.
New JmakProtocolEncoderTest has two tests: testEncodeData for TCP and testEncodeSms for SMS.
With JAVA_HOME set to JDK 25, `./gradlew checkstyleMain checkstyleTest test` ended in BUILD SUCCESSFUL. The test results show 612 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors and 27 skipped.

human_needed.question: Which command type should the JMAK movement alarm (parameter 59) use? I used Command.TYPE_ALARM_GEOFENCE, with the value from KEY_DATA.
human_needed.why: Command.java has no movement alarm type. Meiligao uses alarmGeofence for its movement alarm, but alarmVibration or a new type would also make sense.

human_needed.question: Is the TCP prefix really `$`?
human_needed.why: In the task text, the TCP prefix was replaced by garbled text. I took `$` from the example `$34;1;#`.

harness_used: Skill .claude/skills/add-protocol-decoder: its steps for adding an encoder and registering supported commands

Existing encoders used as patterns: WondexProtocol/WondexProtocolEncoder (text command encoder registration), MeiligaoProtocolEncoder (movement alarm mapped to alarmGeofence), WatchProtocolEncoder (KEY_ENABLE for alarms)

harness_gaps.problem: The skill says to use `make test TESTS=...` and `make check-fast`, but this worktree has no Makefile. I used `./gradlew test --tests ...` and `./gradlew checkstyleMain checkstyleTest test` instead.

The build needs Java 21 or newer (`invalid source release: 21`), but the default JDK on the machine is 17, and nothing in the repo says which JDK to use. I set JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@25 to make it work.
The skill only covers decoders. It has no steps for an encoder that supports both a text (SMS) channel and a data channel, and no encoder test example (verifyEncode with text()).
